extension.dc:title: DNA derived data
extension.name: dnaDerivedData
extension.dc:description: An extension to Occurrence and Event cores to capture information relating to DNA. This extension is based on the MIxS extension for Darwin Core (underway), with additions from GGBN and MIQE standards and recommendations. This definition supports the outcomes documented in Publishing DNA-derived data through biodiversity data platforms (https://doi.org/10.35035/doc-vf1a-nr22). This extension is subject to change, and recommended for early adopters who understand that data remapping may be required as things evolve.

property.name: samp_name
property.label: sample name
property.dc:description: A local identifier or name that for the material sample used for extracting nucleic acids, and subsequent sequencing. It can refer either to the original material collected or to any derived sub-samples. It can have any format, but we suggest that you make it concise, unique and consistent within your lab, and as informative as possible. INSDC requires every sample name from a single Submitter to be unique. Use of a globally unique identifier for the field source_mat_id is recommended in addition to sample_name
property.comments: Sample Name is a name that you choose for the sample. It can have any format, but we suggest that you make it concise, unique and consistent within your lab, and as informative as possible. Every Sample Name from a single Submitter must be unique.

property.name: occurrenceID
property.label: Occurrence ID
property.dc:description: An identifier for a dwc:Occurrence (as opposed to a particular digital record of a dwc:Occurrence).
property.comments: In the absence of a persistent global unique identifier, construct one from a combination of identifiers in the record that will most closely make the dwc:occurrenceID globally unique.

translation.label: Identificador del registro
translation.comments: A falta de un identificador único global persistente, construya uno a partir de una combinación de identificadores del registro que haga que el dwc:occurrenceID sea lo más parecido posible a un identificador único a nivel mundial.
translation.dc:description: Un identificador para una dwc:Occurrence (a diferencia de un registro digital concreto de una dwc:Occurrence).

property.name: project_name
property.label: project name
property.dc:description: Name of the project within which the sequencing was organized

property.name: experimental_factor
property.label: experimental factor
property.dc:description: Variable aspects of an experiment design that can be used to describe an experiment, or set of experiments, in an increasingly detailed manner. This field accepts ontology terms from Experimental Factor Ontology (EFO) and/or Ontology for Biomedical Investigations (OBI)
property.comments: Experimental factors are essentially the variable aspects of an experiment design which can be used to describe an experiment, or set of experiments, in an increasingly detailed manner. This field accepts ontology terms from Experimental Factor Ontology (EFO) and/or Ontology for Biomedical Investigations (OBI). For a browser of EFO (v 2.95) terms, please see http://purl.bioontology.org/ontology/EFO; for a browser of OBI (v 2018-02-12) terms please see http://purl.bioontology.org/ontology/OBI

property.name: samp_taxon_id
property.label: taxonomy ID of DNA sample
property.dc:description: NCBI taxon id of the sample. Maybe be a single taxon or mixed taxa sample. Use 'synthetic metagenome for mock community/positive controls, or 'blank sample' for negative controls
property.comments: NCBI taxon id of the sample. Maybe be a single taxon or mixed taxa sample. Use "synthetic metagenome" for mock community/positive controls, or "blank sample" for negative controls

property.name: neg_cont_type
property.label: negative control type
property.dc:description: The substance or equipment used as a negative control in an investigation

property.name: pos_cont_type
property.label: positive control type
property.dc:description: The substance, mixture, product, or apparatus used to verify that a process which is part of an investigation delivers a true positive

property.name: env_broad_scale
property.label: broad-scale environmental context
property.dc:description: Report the major environmental system the sample or specimen came from. The system(s) identified should have a coarse spatial grain, to provide the general environmental context of where the sampling was done (e.g. in the desert or a rainforest). We recommend using subclasses of EnvO s biome class: http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/ENVO_00000428. EnvO documentation about how to use the field: https://github.com/EnvironmentOntology/envo/wiki/Using-ENVO-with-MIxS
property.comments: In this field, report which major environmental system your sample or specimen came from. The systems identified should have a coarse spatial grain, to provide the general environmental context of where the sampling was done (e.g. were you in the desert or a rainforest?). We recommend using subclasses of ENVO’s biome class: http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/ENVO_00000428. Format (one term): termLabel [termID], Format (multiple terms): termLabel [termID]|termLabel [termID]|termLabel [termID]. Example: Annotating a water sample from the photic zone in middle of the Atlantic Ocean, consider: oceanic epipelagic zone biome [ENVO:01000033]. Example: Annotating a sample from the Amazon rainforest consider: tropical moist broadleaf forest biome [ENVO:01000228]. If needed, request new terms on the ENVO tracker, identified here: http://www.obofoundry.org/ontology/envo.html

property.name: env_local_scale
property.label: local environmental context
property.dc:description: Report the entity or entities which are in the sample or specimen s local vicinity and which you believe have significant causal influences on your sample or specimen. We recommend using EnvO terms which are of smaller spatial grain than your entry for env_broad_scale. Terms, such as anatomical sites, from other OBO Library ontologies which interoperate with EnvO (e.g. UBERON) are accepted in this field. EnvO documentation about how to use the field: https://github.com/EnvironmentOntology/envo/wiki/Using-ENVO-with-MIxS
property.comments: In this field, report the entity or entities which are in your sample or specimen’s local vicinity and which you believe have significant causal influences on your sample or specimen. Please use terms that are present in ENVO and which are of smaller spatial grain than your entry for env_broad_scale. Format (one term): termLabel [termID]; Format (multiple terms): termLabel [termID]|termLabel [termID]|termLabel [termID]. Example: Annotating a pooled sample taken from various vegetation layers in a forest consider: canopy [ENVO:00000047]|herb and fern layer [ENVO:01000337]|litter layer [ENVO:01000338]|understory [01000335]|shrub layer [ENVO:01000336]. If needed, request new terms on the ENVO tracker, identified here: http://www.obofoundry.org/ontology/envo.html

property.name: env_medium
property.label: environmental medium
property.dc:description: Report the environmental material(s) immediately surrounding the sample or specimen at the time of sampling. We recommend using subclasses of 'environmental material' (http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/ENVO_00010483). EnvO documentation about how to use the field: https://github.com/EnvironmentOntology/envo/wiki/Using-ENVO-with-MIxS . Terms from other OBO ontologies are permissible as long as they reference mass/volume nouns (e.g. air, water, blood) and not discrete, countable entities (e.g. a tree, a leaf, a table top)
property.comments: In this field, report which environmental material or materials (pipe separated) immediately surrounded your sample or specimen prior to sampling, using one or more subclasses of ENVO’s environmental material class: http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/ENVO_00010483. Format (one term): termLabel [termID]; Format (multiple terms): termLabel [termID]|termLabel [termID]|termLabel [termID]. Example: Annotating a fish swimming in the upper 100 m of the Atlantic Ocean, consider: ocean water [ENVO:00002151]. Example: Annotating a duck on a pond consider: pond water [ENVO:00002228]|air ENVO_00002005. If needed, request new terms on the ENVO tracker, identified here: http://www.obofoundry.org/ontology/envo.html

property.name: subspecf_gen_lin
property.label: subspecific genetic lineage
property.dc:description: Information about the genetic distinctness of the sequenced organism below the subspecies level, e.g., serovar, serotype, biotype, ecotype, or any relevant genetic typing schemes like Group I plasmid. Subspecies should not be recorded in this term, but in the NCBI taxonomy. Supply both the lineage name and the lineage rank separated by a colon, e.g., biovar:abc123
property.comments: This should provide further information about the genetic distinctness of the sequenced organism by recording additional information e.g. serovar, serotype, biotype, ecotype, or any relevant genetic typing schemes like Group I plasmid. It can also contain alternative taxonomic information. It should contain both the lineage name, and the lineage rank, i.e. biovar:abc123

property.name: ploidy
property.label: ploidy
property.dc:description: The ploidy level of the genome (e.g. allopolyploid, haploid, diploid, triploid, tetraploid). It has implications for the downstream study of duplicated gene and regions of the genomes (and perhaps for difficulties in assembly). For terms, please select terms listed under class ploidy (PATO:001374) of Phenotypic Quality Ontology (PATO), and for a browser of PATO (v 2018-03-27) please refer to http://purl.bioontology.org/ontology/PATO

property.name: num_replicons
property.label: number of replicons
property.dc:description: Reports the number of replicons in a nuclear genome of eukaryotes, in the genome of a bacterium or archaea or the number of segments in a segmented virus. Always applied to the haploid chromosome count of a eukaryote

property.name: extrachrom_elements
property.label: extrachromosomal elements
property.dc:description: Do plasmids exist of significant phenotypic consequence (e.g. ones that determine virulence or antibiotic resistance). Megaplasmids? Other plasmids (borrelia has 15+ plasmids)

property.name: estimated_genome_size
property.label: estimated genome size
property.dc:description: The estimated size of the genome prior to sequencing. Of particular importance in the sequencing of (eukaryotic) genome which could remain in draft form for a long or unspecified period

property.name: ref_biomaterial
property.label: reference for biomaterial
property.dc:description: Primary publication if isolated before genome publication; otherwise, primary genome report

property.name: source_mat_id
property.label: source material identifiers
property.dc:description: A unique identifier assigned to a material sample (as defined by http://rs.tdwg.org/dwc/terms/materialSampleID, and as opposed to a particular digital record of a material sample) used for extracting nucleic acids, and subsequent sequencing. The identifier can refer either to the original material collected or to any derived sub-samples. The INSDC qualifiers /specimen_voucher, /bio_material, or /culture_collection may or may not share the same value as the source_mat_id field. For instance, the /specimen_voucher qualifier and source_mat_id may both contain 'UAM:Herps:14' , referring to both the specimen voucher and sampled tissue with the same identifier. However, the /culture_collection qualifier may refer to a value from an initial culture (e.g. ATCC:11775) while source_mat_id would refer to an identifier from some derived culture from which the nucleic acids were extracted (e.g. xatc123 or ark:/2154/R2)

property.name: pathogenicity
property.label: known pathogenicity
property.dc:description: To what is the entity pathogenic

property.name: biotic_relationship
property.label: observed biotic relationship
property.dc:description: Description of relationship(s) between the subject organism and other organism(s) it is associated with. E.g., parasite on species X; mutualist with species Y. The target organism is the subject of the relationship, and the other organism(s) is the object

property.name: specific_host
property.label: host scientific name
property.dc:description: Report the host's taxonomic name and/or NCBI taxonomy ID
property.comments: If there is a host involved, please provide its taxid (or environmental if not actually isolated from the dead or alive host - i.e. a pathogen could be isolated from a swipe of a bench etc) and report whether it is a laboratory or natural host)

property.name: host_spec_range
property.label: host specificity or range
property.dc:description: The range and diversity of host species that an organism is capable of infecting, defined by NCBI taxonomy identifier
property.comments: The NCBI taxonomy identifier of the specific host if it is known

property.name: host_disease_stat
property.label: host disease status
property.dc:description: List of diseases with which the host has been diagnosed; can include multiple diagnoses. The value of the field depends on host; for humans the terms should be chosen from the DO (Human Disease Ontology) at https://www.disease-ontology.org, non-human host diseases are free text

property.name: trophic_level
property.label: trophic level
property.dc:description: Trophic levels are the feeding position in a food chain. Microbes can be a range of producers (e.g. chemolithotroph)

property.name: propagation
property.label: propagation
property.dc:description: The type of reproduction from the parent stock. Values for this field is specific to different taxa. For phage or virus: lytic/lysogenic/temperate/obligately lytic. For plasmids: incompatibility group. For eukaryotes: sexual/asexual
property.comments: This field is specific to different taxa. For phages: lytic/lysogenic, for plasmids: incompatibility group, for eukaryotes: sexual/asexual (Note: there is the strong opinion to name phage propagation obligately lytic or temperate, therefore we also give this choice

property.name: encoded_traits
property.label: encoded traits
property.dc:description: Should include key traits like antibiotic resistance or xenobiotic degradation phenotypes for plasmids, converting genes for phage

property.name: rel_to_oxygen
property.label: relationship to oxygen
property.dc:description: Is this organism an aerobe, anaerobe? Please note that aerobic and anaerobic are valid descriptors for microbial environments

property.name: isol_growth_condt
property.label: isolation and growth condition
property.dc:description: Publication reference in the form of pubmed ID (pmid), digital object identifier (doi) or url for isolation and growth condition specifications of the organism/material

property.name: samp_collect_device
property.label: sample collection device
property.dc:description: The device used to collect an environmental sample. This field accepts terms listed under environmental sampling device (http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/ENVO). This field also accepts terms listed under specimen collection device (http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GENEPIO_0002094)
property.comments: Recommended best practice is to use a controlled vocabulary such as the entities listed under specimen collection device (http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/OBI_0002814) in the Ontology for Biomedical Investigations.
property.examples: `air filter, malaise trap, niskin bottle, surface swab`

property.name: samp_collect_method
property.label: sample collection method
property.dc:description: The method employed for collecting the sample

property.name: samp_mat_process
property.label: sample material processing
property.dc:description: A brief description of any processing applied to the sample during or after retrieving the sample from environment, or a link to the relevant protocol(s) performed
property.comments: Any processing applied to the sample during or after retrieving the sample from environment. This field accepts OBI, for a browser of OBI (v 2018-02-12) terms please see http://purl.bioontology.org/ontology/OBI
property.examples: `filtering of seawater, storing samples in ethanol`

property.name: size_frac
property.label: size fraction selected
property.dc:description: Filtering pore size used in sample preparation

property.name: samp_size
property.label: amount or size of sample collected
property.dc:description: The total amount or size (volume (ml), mass (g) or area (m2) ) of sample collected
property.comments: Amount or size of sample (volume, mass or area) that was collected

property.name: samp_vol_we_dna_ext
property.label: sample volume or weight for DNA extraction
property.dc:description: Volume (ml) or mass (g) of total collected sample processed for DNA extraction. Note: total sample collected should be entered under the term Sample Size (MIXS:0000001)

property.name: source_uvig
property.label: source of UViGs
property.dc:description: Type of dataset from which the UViG was obtained

property.name: virus_enrich_appr
property.label: virus enrichment approach
property.dc:description: List of approaches used to enrich the sample for viruses, if any

property.name: nucl_acid_ext
property.label: nucleic acid extraction
property.dc:description: A link to a literature reference, electronic resource or a standard operating procedure (SOP), that describes the material separation to recover the nucleic acid fraction from a sample

property.name: nucl_acid_amp
property.label: nucleic acid amplification
property.dc:description: A link to a literature reference, electronic resource or a standard operating procedure (SOP), that describes the enzymatic amplification (PCR, TMA, NASBA) of specific nucleic acids

property.name: lib_size
property.label: library size
property.dc:description: Total number of clones in the library prepared for the project

property.name: lib_reads_seqd
property.label: library reads sequenced
property.dc:description: Total number of clones sequenced from the library

property.name: lib_layout
property.label: library layout
property.dc:description: Specify whether to expect single, paired, or other configuration of reads

property.name: lib_vector
property.label: library vector
property.dc:description: Cloning vector type(s) used in construction of libraries

property.name: lib_screen
property.label: library screening strategy
property.dc:description: Specific enrichment or screening methods applied before and/or after creating libraries

property.name: target_gene
property.label: target gene
property.dc:description: Targeted gene or locus name for marker gene studies

property.name: target_subfragment
property.label: target subfragment
property.dc:description: Name of subfragment of a gene or locus. Important to e.g. identify special regions on marker genes like V6 on 16S rRNA

property.name: pcr_primers
property.label: pcr primers
property.dc:description: PCR primers that were used to amplify the sequence of the targeted gene, locus or subfragment. This field should contain all the primers used for a single PCR reaction if multiple forward or reverse primers are present in a single PCR reaction. The primer sequence should be reported in uppercase letters

property.name: mid
property.label: multiplex identifiers
property.dc:description: Molecular barcodes, called Multiplex Identifiers (MIDs), that are used to specifically tag unique samples in a sequencing run. Sequence should be reported in uppercase letters

property.name: adapters
property.label: adapters
property.dc:description: Adapters provide priming sequences for both amplification and sequencing of the sample-library fragments. Both adapters should be reported; in uppercase letters

property.name: pcr_cond
property.label: pcr conditions
property.dc:description: Description of reaction conditions and components of polymerase chain reaction performed during library preparation.
property.comments: Description of reaction conditions and components of PCR in the form of ´initial denaturation:94degC_1.5min; annealing=...´

property.name: seq_meth
property.label: sequencing method
property.dc:description: Sequencing machine used. Where possible the term should be taken from the OBI list of DNA sequencers (http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/OBI_0400103)
property.comments: Sequencing method used; e.g. Sanger, ABI-solid

property.name: seq_quality_check
property.label: sequence quality check
property.dc:description: Indicate if the sequence has been called by automatic systems (none) or undergone a manual editing procedure (e.g. by inspecting the raw data or chromatograms). Applied only for sequences that are not submitted to SRA,ENA or DRA

property.name: chimera_check
property.label: chimera check software
property.dc:description: Tool(s) used for chimera checking, including version number and parameters, to discover and remove chimeric sequences. A chimeric sequence is comprised of two or more phylogenetically distinct parent sequences
property.comments: A chimeric sequence, or chimera for short, is a sequence comprised of two or more phylogenetically distinct parent sequences. Chimeras are usually PCR artifacts thought to occur when a prematurely terminated amplicon reanneals to a foreign DNA strand and is copied to completion in the following PCR cycles. The point at which the chimeric sequence changes from one parent to the next is called the breakpoint or conversion point

property.name: tax_ident
property.label: taxonomic identity marker
property.dc:description: The phylogenetic marker(s) used to assign an organism name to the SAG or MAG

property.name: assembly_qual
property.label: assembly quality
property.dc:description: The assembly quality category is based on sets of criteria outlined for each assembly quality category. For MISAG/MIMAG; Finished: Single, validated, contiguous sequence per replicon without gaps or ambiguities with a consensus error rate equivalent to Q50 or better. High Quality Draft:Multiple fragments where gaps span repetitive regions. Presence of the large subunit (LSU) RNA, small subunit (SSU) and the presence of 5.8S rRNA or 5S rRNA depending on whether it is a eukaryotic or prokaryotic genome, respectively. Medium Quality Draft:Many fragments with little to no review of assembly other than reporting of standard assembly statistics. Low Quality Draft:Many fragments with little to no review of assembly other than reporting of standard assembly statistics. Assembly statistics include, but are not limited to total assembly size, number of contigs, contig N50/L50, and maximum contig length. For MIUVIG; Finished: Single, validated, contiguous sequence per replicon without gaps or ambiguities, with extensive manual review and editing to annotate putative gene functions and transcriptional units. High-quality draft genome: One or multiple fragments, totaling 90% of the expected genome or replicon sequence or predicted complete. Genome fragment(s): One or multiple fragments, totalling < 90% of the expected genome or replicon sequence, or for which no genome size could be estimated
property.comments: The assembly quality category is based on sets of criteria outlined for each assembly quality category. For MISAG/MIMAG; Finished: Single, validated, contiguous sequence per replicon without gaps or ambiguities with a consensus error rate equivalent to Q50 or better. High Quality Draft:Multiple fragments where gaps span repetitive regions. Presence of the 23S, 16S and 5S rRNA genes and at least 18 tRNAs. Medium Quality Draft:Many fragments with little to no review of assembly other than reporting of standard assembly statistics. Low Quality Draft:Many fragments with little to no review of assembly other than reporting of standard assembly statistics. Assembly statistics include, but are not limited to total assembly size, number of contigs, contig N50/L50, and maximum contig length. For MIUVIG; Finished: Single, validated, contiguous sequence per replicon without gaps or ambiguities, with extensive manual review and editing to annotate putative gene functions and transcriptional units. High-quality draft genome: One or multiple fragments, totaling ≥ 90% of the expected genome or replicon sequence or predicted complete. Genome fragment(s): One or multiple fragments, totalling < 90% of the expected genome or replicon sequence, or for which no genome size could be estimated

property.name: assembly_name
property.label: assembly name
property.dc:description: Name/version of the assembly provided by the submitter that is used in the genome browsers and in the community

property.name: assembly_software
property.label: assembly software
property.dc:description: Tool(s) used for assembly, including version number and parameters

property.name: annot
property.label: annotation
property.dc:description: Tool used for annotation, or for cases where annotation was provided by a community jamboree or model organism database rather than by a specific submitter

property.name: number_contig
property.label: number of contigs
property.dc:description: Total number of contigs in the cleaned/submitted assembly that makes up a given genome, SAG, MAG, or UViG

property.name: feat_pred
property.label: feature prediction
property.dc:description: Method used to predict UViGs features such as ORFs, integration site, etc

property.name: ref_db
property.label: reference database(s)
property.dc:description: List of database(s) used for ORF annotation, along with version number and reference to website or publication

property.name: sim_search_meth
property.label: similarity search method
property.dc:description: Tool used to compare ORFs with database, along with version and cutoffs used

property.name: tax_class
property.label: taxonomic classification
property.dc:description: Method used for taxonomic classification, along with reference database used, classification rank, and thresholds used to classify new genomes
property.examples: `vConTACT vContact2 (references from NCBI RefSeq v83, genus rank classification, default parameters)`

property.name: x16s_recover
property.label: 16S recovered
property.dc:description: Can a 16S gene be recovered from the submitted SAG or MAG?

property.name: x16s_recover_software
property.label: 16S recovery software
property.dc:description: Tools used for 16S rRNA gene extraction

property.name: trnas
property.label: number of standard tRNAs extracted
property.dc:description: The total number of tRNAs identified from the SAG or MAG

property.name: trna_ext_software
property.label: tRNA extraction software
property.dc:description: Tools used for tRNA identification

property.name: compl_score
property.label: completeness score
property.dc:description: Completeness score is typically based on either the fraction of markers found as compared to a database or the percent of a genome found as compared to a closely related reference genome. High Quality Draft: >90%, Medium Quality Draft: >50%, and Low Quality Draft: < 50% should have the indicated completeness scores

property.name: compl_software
property.label: completeness software
property.dc:description: Tools used for completion estimate, i.e. checkm, anvi'o, busco

property.name: compl_appr
property.label: completeness approach
property.dc:description: The approach used to determine the completeness of a given genomic assembly, which would typically make use of a set of conserved marker genes or a closely related reference genome. For UViG completeness, include reference genome or group used, and contig feature suggesting a complete genome
property.comments: The approach used to determine the completeness of a given SAG or MAG, which would typically make use of a set of conserved marker genes or a closely related reference genome. For UViG completeness, include reference genome or group used, and contig feature suggesting a complete genome
property.examples: `other: UViG length compared to the average length of reference genomes from the P22virus genus (NCBI RefSeq v83)`

property.name: contam_score
property.label: contamination score
property.dc:description: The contamination score is based on the fraction of single-copy genes that are observed more than once in a query genome. The following scores are acceptable for; High Quality Draft: < 5%, Medium Quality Draft: < 10%, Low Quality Draft: < 10%. Contamination must be below 5% for a SAG or MAG to be deposited into any of the public databases

property.name: contam_screen_input
property.label: contamination screening input
property.dc:description: The type of sequence data used as input

property.name: contam_screen_param
property.label: contamination screening parameters
property.dc:description: Specific parameters used in the decontamination sofware, such as reference database, coverage, and kmers. Combinations of these parameters may also be used, i.e. kmer and coverage, or reference database and kmer

property.name: decontam_software
property.label: decontamination software
property.dc:description: Tool(s) used in contamination screening

property.name: sort_tech
property.label: sorting technology
property.dc:description: Method used to sort/isolate cells or particles of interest

property.name: sc_lysis_approach
property.label: single cell or viral particle lysis approach
property.dc:description: Method used to free DNA from interior of the cell(s) or particle(s)

property.name: sc_lysis_method
property.label: single cell or viral particle lysis kit protocol
property.dc:description: Name of the kit or standard protocol used for cell(s) or particle(s) lysis

property.name: wga_amp_appr
property.label: WGA amplification approach
property.dc:description: Method used to amplify genomic DNA in preparation for sequencing

property.name: wga_amp_kit
property.label: WGA amplification kit
property.dc:description: Kit used to amplify genomic DNA in preparation for sequencing

property.name: bin_param
property.label: binning parameters
property.dc:description: The parameters that have been applied during the extraction of genomes from metagenomic datasets

property.name: bin_software
property.label: binning software
property.dc:description: Tool(s) used for the extraction of genomes from metagenomic datasets, where possible include a product ID (PID) of the tool(s) used

property.name: reassembly_bin
property.label: reassembly post binning
property.dc:description: Has an assembly been performed on a genome bin extracted from a metagenomic assembly?

property.name: mag_cov_software
property.label: MAG coverage software
property.dc:description: Tool(s) used to determine the genome coverage if coverage is used as a binning parameter in the extraction of genomes from metagenomic datasets

property.name: vir_ident_software
property.label: viral identification software
property.dc:description: Tool(s) used for the identification of UViG as a viral genome, software or protocol name including version number, parameters, and cutoffs used

property.name: pred_genome_type
property.label: predicted genome type
property.dc:description: Type of genome predicted for the UViG

property.name: pred_genome_struc
property.label: predicted genome structure
property.dc:description: Expected structure of the viral genome

property.name: detec_type
property.label: detection type
property.dc:description: Type of UViG detection

property.name: otu_class_appr
property.label: OTU classification approach
property.dc:description: Cutoffs and approach used when clustering species-level OTUs. Note that results from standard 95% ANI / 85% AF clustering should be provided alongside OTUs defined from another set of thresholds, even if the latter are the ones primarily used during the analysis
property.comments: Cutoffs and approach used when clustering new UViGs in "species-level" OTUs. Note that results from standard 95% ANI / 85% AF clustering should be provided alongside OTUS defined from another set of thresholds, even if the latter are the ones primarily used during the analysis

property.name: otu_seq_comp_appr
property.label: OTU sequence comparison approach
property.dc:description: Tool and thresholds used to compare sequences when computing "species-level" OTUs

property.name: otu_db
property.label: OTU database
property.dc:description: Reference database (i.e. sequences not generated as part of the current study) used to cluster new genomes in "species-level" OTUs, if any

property.name: host_pred_appr
property.label: host prediction approach
property.dc:description: Tool or approach used for host prediction

property.name: host_pred_est_acc
property.label: host prediction estimated accuracy
property.dc:description: For each tool or approach used for host prediction, estimated false discovery rates should be included, either computed de novo or from the literature
property.examples: `CRISPR spacer match: 0 or 1 mismatches, estimated 8% FDR at the host genus rank (Edwards et al. 2016 doi:10.1093/femsre/fuv048)`

property.name: associated_resource
property.label: relevant electronic resources
property.dc:description: A related resource that is referenced, cited, or otherwise associated to the sequence

property.name: sop
property.label: relevant standard operating procedures
property.dc:description: Standard operating procedures used in assembly and/or annotation of genomes, metagenomes or environmental sequences

property.name: pcr_primer_forward
property.label: PCR Primer Forward
property.dc:description: Forward PCR primer that were used to amplify the sequence of the targeted gene, locus or subfragment. If multiple multiple forward or reverse primers are present in a single PCR reaction, there should be a full row for each of these linked to the same DWC Occurrence. The primer sequence should be reported in uppercase letters

property.name: pcr_primer_reverse
property.label: PCR Primer Reverse
property.dc:description: Reverse PCR primer that were used to amplify the sequence of the targeted gene, locus or subfragment. If multiple multiple forward or reverse primers are present in a single PCR reaction, there should be a full row for each of these linked to the same DWC Occurrence. The primer sequence should be reported in uppercase letters

property.name: pcr_primer_name_forward
property.label: PCR Primer Name Forward
property.dc:description: Name of the forward PCR primer that were used to amplify the sequence of the targeted gene, locus or subfragment. If multiple multiple forward or reverse primers are present in a single PCR reaction, there should be a full row for each of these linked to the same DWC Occurrence.

property.name: pcr_primer_name_reverse
property.label: PCR Primer Name Reverse
property.dc:description: Name of the reverse PCR primer that were used to amplify the sequence of the targeted gene, locus or subfragment. If multiple multiple forward or reverse primers are present in a single PCR reaction, there should be a full row for each of these linked to the same DWC Occurrence.

property.name: pcr_primer_reference
property.label: PCR Primer Reference
property.dc:description: Reference for the PCR primers that were used to amplify the sequence of the targeted gene, locus or subfragment.

property.name: DNA_sequence
property.label: DNA Sequence
property.dc:description: The DNA sequence

property.name: concentration
property.label: Concentration
property.dc:description: Concentration of DNA (weight ng/volume µl)

property.name: concentrationUnit
property.label: Concentration Unit
property.dc:description: Unit used for concentration measurement

property.name: methodDeterminationConcentrationAndRatios
property.label: Method Determination Concentration And Ratios
property.dc:description: Description of method used for concentration measurement

property.name: ratioOfAbsorbance260_230
property.label: Ratio Of Absorbance 260/230
property.dc:description: Ratio of absorbance at 260 nm and 230 nm assessing DNA purity (mostly secondary measure, indicates mainly EDTA, carbohydrates, phenol), (DNA samples only).

property.name: ratioOfAbsorbance260_280
property.label: Ratio Of Absorbance 260/280
property.dc:description: Ratio of absorbance at 260 nm and 280 nm assessing DNA purity (mostly secondary measure, indicates mainly EDTA, carbohydrates, phenol), (DNA samples only).

property.name: annealingTemp
property.label: Annealing Temperature
property.dc:description: The reaction temperature during the annealing phase of PCR.

property.name: annealingTempUnit
property.label: Annealing Temperature Unit
property.dc:description: Measurement unit of the reaction temperature during the annealing phase of PCR.

property.name: probeReporter
property.label: Probe Reporter
property.dc:description: Type of fluorophore (reporter) used. Probe anneals within amplified target DNA. Polymerase activity degrades the probe that has annealed to the template, and the probe releases the fluorophore from it and breaks the proximity to the quencher, thus allowing fluorescence of the fluorophore.

property.name: probeQuencher
property.label: Probe Quencher
property.dc:description: Type of quencher used. The quencher molecule quenches the fluorescence emitted by the fluorophore when excited by the cycler’s light source As long as fluorophore and the quencher are in proximity, quenching inhibits any fluorescence signals.

property.name: ampliconSize
property.label: Amplicon Size
property.dc:description: The length of the amplicon in basepairs.

property.name: thresholdQuantificationCycle
property.label: Threshold Quantification Cycle
property.dc:description: Threshold for change in fluorescence signal between cycles

property.name: baselineValue
property.label: Baseline Value
property.dc:description: The number of cycles when fluorescence signal from the target amplification is below background fluorescence not originated from the real target amplification.

property.name: quantificationCycle
property.label: Quantification Cycle
property.dc:description: The number of cycles required for the fluorescent signal to cross a given value threshold above the baseline. Quantification cycle (Cq), threshold cycle (Ct), crossing point (Cp), and take-off point (TOP) refer to the same value from the real-time instrument.
property.comments: Use of quantification cycle (Cq), is preferable according to the RDML (Real-Time PCR Data Markup Language) data standard (http://www.rdml.org).

property.name: automaticThresholdQuantificationCycle
property.label: Automatic Threshold Quantification Cycle
property.dc:description: Whether the threshold was set by the instrument or manually.

property.name: automaticBaselineValue
property.label: Automatic Baseline Value
property.dc:description: Whether the baseline value was set by the instrument or manually.

property.name: contaminationAssessment
property.label: Contamination Assessment
property.dc:description: Whether DNA or RNA contamination assessment was done or not.

property.name: partitionVolume
property.label: Partition Volume
property.dc:description: An accurate estimation of partition volume. The sum of the partitions multiplied by the partition volume will enable the total volume of the reaction to be calculated.

property.name: partitionVolumeUnit
property.label: Partition Volume Unit
property.dc:description: Unit used for partition volume

property.name: estimatedNumberOfCopies
property.label: Estimated Number Of Copies
property.dc:description: Number of target molecules per µl. Mean copies per partition (?) can be calculated using the number of partitions (n) and the estimated copy number in the total volume of all partitions (m) with a formula ?=m/n.

property.name: amplificationReactionVolume
property.label: Amplification Reaction Volume
property.dc:description: PCR reaction volume

property.name: amplificationReactionVolumeUnit
property.label: Amplification Reaction Volume Unit
property.dc:description: Unit used for PCR reaction volume. Many of the instruments require preparation of a much larger initial sample volume than is actually analyzed.

property.name: pcr_analysis_software
property.label: PCR Analysis Software
property.dc:description: The program used to analyse the d(d)PCR runs.

property.name: experimentalVariance
property.label: Experimental Variance
property.dc:description: Multiple biological replicates are encouraged to assess total experimental variation. When single dPCR experiments are performed, a minimal estimate of variance due to counting error alone must be calculated from the binomial (or suitable equivalent) distribution.

property.name: pcr_primer_lod
property.label: PCR Primer Limit Of Detection
property.dc:description: The assay’s ability to detect the target at low levels.

property.name: pcr_primer_loq
property.label: PCR Primer Limit Of Quantification
property.dc:description: The assay’s ability to quantify copy number at low levels.
